A.explanation: Too small. It does not follow $p = F/A$ with the pressure from the $800\text{ N}$ on $8\text{ cm}^2$ acting on $12\text{ cm}^2$.

B.explanation: This uses the inverse area ratio $800 \times 8/12$. Larger brake piston area gives larger force for the same pressure, not smaller.

C.explanation: Same liquid pressure acts on the $12\text{ cm}^2$ piston, giving $F = p \times 12\text{ cm}^2 = 1200\text{ N}$.

D.explanation: This is $4 \times 1200\text{ N}$, the total for all four wheels combined, not the force applied to each brake.

hints: Notice the pedal piston area is $8\text{ cm}^2$ with $800\text{ N}$ on it, while each brake piston area is $12\text{ cm}^2$.
Recall pressure in the incompressible liquid is the same everywhere, with $p = F/A$ at the pedal piston and $F = pA$ at each brake piston.
First calculate $p$ from $800\text{ N}$ and $8\text{ cm}^2$, then multiply that same $p$ by $12\text{ cm}^2$ for one brake - do not divide by 4.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: pedal force $F_1 = 800\text{ N}$, pedal area $A_1 = 8\text{ cm}^2$, each brake area $A_2 = 12\text{ cm}^2$.
State the rule: incompressible liquid transmits pressure unchanged, so $p = F_1/A_1$ at the pedal equals $p = F_2/A_2$ at each brake.
Apply the same pressure to one brake piston: $F_2 = p \times A_2 = 100 \times 12 = 1200\text{ N}$.
Check units and sense: $\text{N cm}^{-2} \times \text{cm}^2 = \text{N}$, and force is larger because brake area is larger than pedal area. This is option C
